text: et suis temporibus exhibuit, videlicet suum sermonem praeconio promulgandum, quod praeconium mihi Servatoris nostri Dei mandato commissum est,
note: *Servātōris nostrī Deī* (τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ, NRSV \"God our Savior\"): *Servātor* capital for God or Christ (decision 20), as your Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 of 7; only Luke 1:47 *Deō servātōre meō* lower); *est,* with a comma, as 1573 (*mandato commiſſum eſt , 4 Tito germano*, canvas 915), for the draft's full stop: 1:1–4 is one sentence, the address running on to the greeting of 1:4 (as Gal 1:1–3); *et* lower case, the sentence of 1:1–2 running on (written here, as a capital changed in a layout line stops the pipeline's own lowering) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Tito germano, quod ad communem fidem attinet, filio, gratiam, misericordiam, pacem a Deo Patre, et Domino Jesu Christo Servatore nostro.
note: *Patre* capital, God the Father (ἀπὸ θεοῦ πατρὸς, decision 20), as your Gal 1:3, 1 Cor 1:3 *ā Deō Patre*; *Patre,* with 1573's comma (*à Deo patre , & Domino*, canvas 915), as your Gal 1:3 *ā Deō Patre, et Dominō*; *Servātōre nostrō* capital, Christ (Χριστοῦ Ἰησοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν): *Servātor* capital for God or Christ (decision 20), as your Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 of 7; only Luke 1:47 *Deō servātōre meō* lower); *Titō* keeps its capital (a name), *grātiam* lower case inside the sentence as 1573 (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Dixit eorum quidam, proprius ipsorum vates: “Cres semper mendax, mala bestia, venter iners est.”
note: the Cretan poet's line (Epimenides, as 1573's margin note *a Epimenides, qui fuit ipse Cretensis*, stage 2) after *Dīxit … vātēs:* in “…”, direct words (BSB “Cretans are always liars …”); no \\qt, not Scripture, as your 1 Cor 15:33 *“Mōrēs bonōs colloquia corrumpunt mala.”* (Menander) and Acts 17:28 (Aratus, in ‘…’ inside Paul's speech); *Crēs* keeps 1573's capital (*vates : … Cres ſemper mendax*, canvas 915) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Puris quidem pura sunt omnia: sed pollutis et infidelibus nihil purum: quin polluta est eorum et mens et conscientia.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 1:14 ends the charge to rebuke the Cretans, and *Pūrīs quidem pūra sunt omnia* opens a new step, the maxim on purity turned against the deceivers (1:15–16) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: frugi, castas, domi manentes, bonas, suis viris obedientes, ne divina doctrina male audiat.
note: *frūgī* lower case: the list of 2:4 (*doceant … amantēs esse,*) runs on, the draft's capital being the line's start only (1573 *frugi, caſtas, domi manentes*, canvas 915); the pipeline did not lower it (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: sed summam fidem bene praestantes, quo Servatoris nostri Dei doctrinam cohonestent in omnibus.
note: *Servātōris nostrī Deī* (τὴν διδασκαλίαν τὴν τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ): *Servātor* capital for God or Christ (decision 20), as your Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 of 7; only Luke 1:47 *Deō servātōre meō* lower); *sed* lower case, the sentence of 2:9 running on (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: exspectantes speratam beatitudinem, adventumque gloriosum magni Dei, et Servatoris nostri Jesu Christi,
note: *Servātōris nostrī Jēsū Chrīstī* (σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ): *Servātor* capital for God or Christ (decision 20), as your Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 of 7; only Luke 1:47 *Deō servātōre meō* lower); *exspectantēs* lower case, the sentence of 2:11–12 running on (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Haec loquere, et exhortare, et argue summa cum auctoritate, ita ut nemo te contemnat.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): *Hæc loquere* closes the chapter with a summary charge to Titus, back from the doctrine of 2:11–14 to his task, as 2:1 *Tū vērō loquere* opened it (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Fuimus enim aliquando nos quoque dementes, contumaces, errantes, variis servientes cupiditatibus et voluptatibus, in pravitate invidiaque degentes, odiosi, alii aliis infensi.
note: paragraph (the BSB's break): 3:2 ends the charge, and *Fuimus enim aliquandō nōs quoque* opens its ground, what we were and how God saved us (3:3–7); the BSB's second break at 3:4 *Sed postquam* left inside it (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Sed postquam benignitas et humanitas exstitit Servatoris nostri Dei,
note: *Servātōris nostrī Deī* (τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν θεοῦ): *Servātor* capital for God or Christ (decision 20), as your Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 of 7; only Luke 1:47 *Deō servātōre meō* lower) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: quo nos large perfudit per Jesum Christum Servatorem nostrum,
note: *Servātōrem nostrum*, Christ (διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν): *Servātor* capital for God or Christ (decision 20), as your Eph 5:23 *Servātor*, Phil 3:20, Luke 2:11, John 4:42, Acts 5:31 and 13:23 *Servātōrem* (6 of 7; only Luke 1:47 *Deō servātōre meō* lower); *quō* lower case, the sentence of 3:4–5 running on (its antecedent the *Spīritūs Sānctī* of 3:5, after stage 2 moved the verse boundary) (Claude, 2026-11-11)

text: Salutant te mei comites omnes. Saluta eos, qui nos amant in fide. Adsit vobis omnibus gratia: Amen. \\cls Scripta Nicopoli Macedoniae.
note: the subscription set apart as \\cls after the verse (decision 37), as 1573 sets it in italics under the verse (*Scripta Nicopoli Macedoniæ.*, canvas 915) and as Gal 6:18, Col 4:18; a full stop after it, as 1573; *grātia: Āmēn.* with 1573's colon (*omnibus gratia : Amen .*), as Col 4:18 and Eph 6:24 (Claude, 2026-11-11)
